extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates / graduate students learning algebraic geometry and sheaf theory
extracted.subtask_description: Textbook chapter and exercises about sheaves: recovering sheaves from their values on a base, morphisms, gluing, abelian-category properties of (abelian) sheaves and OX-modules, inverse image functor, supports, and related constructions. Includes many exercises to verify the stated criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf on a base (base identity and base gluability axioms)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sheaf of sets (or abelian groups, rings, ...) on a base {Bi} consists of the sets F(Bi) and restriction maps resBj,Bi whenever Bi ⊂ Bj satisfying resBk,Bi = resBj,Bi ◦ resBk,Bj, together with: (1) the base identity axiom: if B = ⋃Bi and f,g ∈ F(B) satisfy resB,Bi f = resB,Bi g for all i then f = g; and (2) the base gluability axiom: if B = ⋃Bi and fi ∈ F(Bi) agree on basic opens contained in Bi ∩ Bj, then there exists f ∈ F(B) with resB,Bi f = fi for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the definition of a presheaf on a base plus the two sheaf axioms restricted to the base. The text remarks this is a useful and sometimes confusing way to package the minimal information needed to recover germs and compatibility data. Exercises ask to verify the details and to treat B as always in the base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovering a sheaf from its restriction to a base
rubrics_metrics.description: The data ({F(Bi)}, {resBi,Bj}) for a base {Bi} determine the entire sheaf F: stalks are colimits over Bi containing a point, compatibility of germs can be tested using sections on basic opens, and one can define F(U) as compatible families of germs coming from some basic neighborhoods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 2.5.1: given a sheaf on a base there is a unique (up to unique isomorphism) sheaf extending it. Exercises (2.5.A, 2.5.B) ask to make this precise and verify injectivity/surjectivity of the natural maps F(B) → F(B) (the sheaf built from germs). The central insight: partial information on a base suffices to understand germs and compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of sheaves correspond to morphisms on a base
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of sheaves is determined by the induced collection of maps on the base F(Bi) → G(Bi) commuting with restriction maps; conversely a morphism of sheaves on the base gives a morphism of the induced sheaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.5.C: (a) verify a morphism of sheaves is determined by its induced morphism on the base; (b) show a morphism on the base produces a morphism of the sheafifications (hint: compatible stalks). This yields an equivalence (up to unique isomorphism) between sheaves on X and sheaves on a given base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surjectivity on a base implies epimorphism of sheaves (sufficient criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a morphism F → G of sheaves is surjective on sections over each element Bi of a base (i.e., F(Bi) → G(Bi) is surjective for all i), then the corresponding morphism of sheaves is an epimorphism (surjective). The converse need not hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.5.D and the discussion: this is a useful sufficient criterion for 'surjectivity'. Example: exponential map exp: OX → OX* on X = C can be shown surjective using the base of contractible open sets. Warning: unlike injectivity, the converse (epimorphism implies surjective on base) is false.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing sheaves from local isomorphisms with cocycle condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an open cover X = ⋃Ui and sheaves Fi on Ui together with isomorphisms φij : Fi|Ui∩Uj ≃ Fj|Ui∩Uj that satisfy the cocycle condition φjk ◦ φij = φik on triple overlaps, the Fi can be glued to form a sheaf F on X, unique up to unique isomorphism, with F|Ui ≃ Fi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.5.E: do not assume the cover is finite (so induction may fail); a recommended base is the open sets contained in some Ui. The hypothesis φii = identity is extraneous (follows from cocycle condition). This formalizes 'gluing' constructions and warns about infinite covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaves of abelian groups form an abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: The category Ab_X of sheaves of abelian groups on X is an abelian category: kernels and cokernels exist (kernel presheaf is a sheaf; cokernel is sheafification of presheaf cokernel), images and coimages behave appropriately, and these properties can be checked on stalks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 2.6.2: everything reduces to checking at the level of stalks where abelian-group behavior applies. The text outlines the universal property for cokernels via sheafification and uses exercises to verify the details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalks commute with kernel/cokernel/image (checking morphism properties on stalks)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a morphism φ: F → G of sheaves of abelian groups, (ker φ)_p ≅ ker(F_p → G_p), (coker φ)_p ≅ coker(F_p → G_p), and the image sheaf im φ is the sheafification of the image presheaf with (im φ)_p equal to the image of F_p → G_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 2.6.A, 2.6.B, 2.6.C: use colimit/stalk descriptions and sheafification facts. Consequence: monomorphism/epimorphism and exactness can be checked stalkwise (refer also to Exercises 2.4.M and 2.4.N).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness of sequences of sheaves can be checked on stalks / stalk functor exact
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking the stalk at a point p is an exact functor Ab_X → Ab (i.e., exactness of a sequence of sheaves is equivalent to exactness of the induced sequences on all stalks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.6.D: proves the stalk functor is exact. Use this fact repeatedly when verifying properties of kernels, cokernels, images, and inverse image functors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections-over-U functor is left-exact but not exact
rubrics_metrics.description: For an open U, the functor F ↦ F(U) is left-exact: 0 → F → G → H exact implies 0 → F(U) → G(U) → H(U) is exact, but the sequence need not be right-exact (i.e., surjectivity may fail on global sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.6.F: show left-exactness directly; construct counterexamples to exactness (e.g., the exponential exact sequence 0 → Z → O_X → O_X^* → 1) to see failure of surjectivity on sections. This highlights global-to-local pathologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward (direct image) is left-exact
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 → F → G → H is exact on X and π: X → Y is continuous, then 0 → π_*F → π_*G → π_*H is exact on Y; i.e., the pushforward functor π_* is left-exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.6.G: interpret the global-section functor as the special case Y = point. The exercise suggests using exactness checks on stalks or the left-exactness of section functors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom functors are left-exact in appropriate variance
rubrics_metrics.description: For sheaves of abelian groups, Hom(·,F) is a left-exact contravariant functor and Hom(F,·) is a left-exact covariant functor on Ab_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.6.H: parallels module-category Hom exactness properties (cf. earlier module exercises). Use standard abelian-category arguments to verify left-exactness in the stated variance.

rubrics_metrics.name: OX-modules form an abelian category (analogous properties carry over)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ringed space (X, OX), the category of OX-modules is abelian: exactness and abelian-categorical notions for OX-modules agree with those of the underlying sheaves of abelian groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.6.I and following remarks: many earlier statements for sheaves of abelian groups apply verbatim to OX-modules because exactness is tested on underlying sheaves. One should be able to adapt exercises (e.g., Hom left-exactness) to the OX-module setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product of OX-modules (construction and stalk property)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define tensor product of OX-modules categorically (and construct it explicitly by taking the presheaf tensor product and sheafifying). The tensor product of stalks equals the stalk of the tensor product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.6.J: (a) give categorical definition and explicit construction (presheaf tensor then sheafify); (b) show (M ⊗_OX N)_p ≅ M_p ⊗_{OX,p} N_p. Hint: sheafification can be necessary; an example showing necessity will appear later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse image sheaf π^{-1} as left adjoint to π_* (definition and construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the inverse image functor π^{-1} from sheaves on Y to sheaves on X as the left adjoint to π_*: Mor_X(π^{-1}G, F) ≅ Mor_Y(G, π_*F). Concretely construct π^{-1} by first defining π^{-1}_{pre}G(U) = colim_{V ⊃ π(U)} G(V) and then sheafifying: π^{-1}G := (π^{-1}_{pre}G)^sh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 2.7.1 (adjoint) and Construction 2.7.2 (colimit then sheafify). Exercises point out π^{-1}_{pre} needn't be a sheaf and that sheafification fixes this. The adjunction yields canonical maps π^{-1}π_* → id and id → π_*π^{-1} as usual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjunction bijection characterizing π^{-1} and π_*
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuous π: X → Y and sheaves F on X, G on Y, there is a natural bijection Mor_X(π^{-1}G, F) ≅ Mor_Y(G, π_*F) which is functorial (natural) in both F and G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.7.B: prove the adjunction either via the universal property or using an explicit description of compatible collections of maps φ_{V,U}: G(V) → F(U) for V ⊃ π(U). The bijection is the defining universal property of π^{-1}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalks of inverse image and preservation by π^{-1}
rubrics_metrics.description: For π(p)=q, there is a natural isomorphism (π^{-1}G)_p ≅ G_q: π^{-1} preserves stalks in the evident way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.7.C: construct the isomorphism using colimit descriptions of stalks or via adjointness. This fact is used to show exactness of π^{-1} (by checking on stalks).

rubrics_metrics.name: π^{-1} is exact (for abelian sheaves)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inverse image functor π^{-1} is an exact functor from sheaves of abelian groups on Y to sheaves on X (exactness can be checked on stalks and stalks are preserved by π^{-1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.7.E: use that exactness is stalk-local and that (π^{-1}G)_p ≅ G_q. Remark: π^{-1} is a left adjoint hence right-exact in general, but left-exactness here holds because colimits over filtered index sets of abelian groups are exact (see Exercise 1.6.L).

rubrics_metrics.name: Push-pull (base-change) map construction and functoriality
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a commutative diagram W --α'→ X --α→ Y and β': W → Z, β: X → Z (not necessarily Cartesian), define the push-pull map β^{-1} α_* F → α'_* (β')^{-1} F for a sheaf F on X by adjointness starting from the identity on (β')^{-1}F and using the commutativity of the diagram; the construction is functorial in F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2.7.4 describes the steps via adjointness ((β')^{-1}, (β')_*) and ((α')^{-1}, (α')_*). Exercise 2.7.F asks to show a 'dual' route yields the same map. The construction generalizes to O-modules and cohomology later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of support of a section and of a sheaf (stalk-local notion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sheaf F (or separated presheaf) and s ∈ F(X), define Supp s := { p ∈ X : s_p ≠ 0 in F_p }. For a sheaf G, define Supp G := { p ∈ X : |G_p| ≠ 0 } (i.e., stalk not initial object).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2.7.6: support is stalk-local and thus commutes with restriction. Exercise 2.7.G: show Supp s is closed. Caution 2.7.7 distinguishes the locus where the value of a continuous function is nonzero (open) from where its germ is nonzero (closed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction to closed subset and sheaves supported on closed sets
rubrics_metrics.description: If i: Z → Y is the inclusion of a closed subset Z, then for a sheaf G on Y supported on Z, the natural map G → i_* i^{-1} G is an isomorphism; equivalently, a sheaf supported on a closed subset can be considered as a sheaf on that closed subset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.7.H: show (i_* i^{-1} G)_q is empty if q ∉ Z and equals G_q for q ∈ Z, establishing the equivalence. This identifies sheaves supported on closed sets with sheaves on the closed subset via pushforward/restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension by zero as occasional left adjoint to inverse image for open inclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: When π is the inclusion of an open subset U ↪ Y, the inverse image π^{-1} sometimes admits a right (or left in some contexts) adjoint called extension by zero; this will be discussed where needed (reference to later section 23.4.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2.7.8 remarks that in addition to always being a left adjoint, π^{-1} can sometimes be a right adjoint in the special case of open inclusions—details deferred until needed. This is a situational adjunction (extension-by-zero) rather than a general property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monomorphism/epimorphism and other morphism properties are stalk-local
rubrics_metrics.description: Properties such as being a monomorphism or an epimorphism of sheaves are determined at the level of stalks (i.e., a map is mono/epi iff it is so on all stalks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text references Exercises 2.4.M and 2.4.N and notes that many abelian-category notions for sheaves may be checked stalk-by-stalk. This motivates checking algebraic properties locally via stalks rather than globally.
